item.content:encoded:
More than 160 taekwondo athletes from across Fiji are battling for national honours today as the Fiji Taekwondo Association President's Cup 2026 and the 15th Fiji National Championship gets underway at the Kshatriya Hall in Suva.

The competition has attracted 163 athletes from nine clubs around the country, with women making up 43 percent of the participants, highlighting the growing popularity and inclusiveness of the sport in Fiji.

Opening the championship this morning, Minister for Education Aseri Radrodro says the event provides young athletes with an important opportunity to develop their skills while also serving as part of the pathway to the 2027 Pacific Games.

Radrodro says education is not only about academic achievement but also about preparing young people for life by developing discipline, resilience, leadership, teamwork and respect.

Meanwhile, the competition is also the first national selection trial on the pathway to the 2027 Pacific Games in Tahiti.

Stay with us as we bring you the results from the competition.

item.title: McCutcheon sets personal best at Commonwealth Games, advances to semis
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 25/07/2026 16-year-old Anahira McCutcheon clocked a personal best to finish fourth in the women's 50-metre butterfly heats last night at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 25/07/2026

16-year-old Anahira McCutcheon clocked a personal best to finish fourth in the women's 50-metre butterfly heats last night at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games.

She recorded a time of 27.09 seconds to qualify for the semi-finals at 9.30pm.

Meanwhile, Don Younger finished fourth in the men's 100-metre breaststroke heats, while Samuel Yalimaiwai placed fifth.

In boxing, Team Fiji's Ben Maukakala lost to New Zealand's Connor Campbell in the men's 65kg preliminary bout.

In basketball, Fiji's women's 3x3 team went down 16–14 to Kenya.

Coming up today, Fiji's men's 3x3 basketball team will take on Malaysia at 9pm.

In swimming, Tolu Young will compete in the men's 50-metre freestyle heats, while Kelera Mudunakaso will contest the women's 100-metre breaststroke heats. The swimming session begins at 9.30pm.

In boxing, Jone Davule will compete in the men's 60kg division, while Aminiasi Saratibau will feature in the men's 80kg division. The boxing programme gets underway at 10pm.

item.title: Grammar to defend Southern Zone Deans crown against Nasinu
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 24/07/2026 The Suva Grammar School Under-18 side will be looking to retain its Vodafone Deans Southern Zone Secondary Schools Rugby Union title tomorrow when it takes on Nasinu Secondary School in the final.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 24/07/2026

The Suva Grammar School Under-18 side will be looking to retain its Vodafone Deans Southern Zone Secondary Schools Rugby Union title tomorrow when it takes on Nasinu Secondary School in the final.

Grammar is the defending champion after defeating rivals Marist Brothers High School 15-13 in last year's final.

This year, the side faces Nasinu Secondary School, which has been a force to be reckoned with throughout the round-robin stage.

Nasinu has been consistent throughout this year's competition, but Grammar is unlikely to surrender the title without a fight.

Grammar will also feature in four other finals.

The Under-14 side will face MGM High School, the Under-17 team will take on Gospel High School, the Under-19 side will meet Nasinu Secondary School, while the Under-16 Raluve team will also face Nasinu Secondary School.

The Southern Zone finals will be held at Grammar Grounds and Veiuto Ground tomorrow.

item.title: Drua women ready to leave it all on the field in historic Super W final - Tawake
item.description: The McDonald's Fiji Drua Women's team is just one sleep away from the Super W Grand Final, and captain Bitala Tawake says the players are determined to leave everything on the field when they take on their opponents tomorrow. Speaking from their home base in Nadi,Tawake says the team has worked hard throughout the season and is ready to give their all in front of their home fans.
item.content:encoded:
The McDonald's Fiji Drua Women's team is just one sleep away from the Super W Grand Final, and captain Bitala Tawake says the players are determined to leave everything on the field when they take on their opponents tomorrow.

Speaking from their home base in Nadi,Tawake says the team has worked hard throughout the season and is ready to give their all in front of their home fans.

The daughter of former Navy Commander Humphrey Tawake will marshal the Fijian Drua into their first-ever Super W Grand Final to be played on home soil, marking a significant milestone for the club and women's rugby in Fiji.

Tawake says the players are fully focused on the task ahead and are committed to delivering a performance that reflects the sacrifice and hard work they have put in to reach the final.

She says the team can not wait to hear the fans' cheering and feel their energy at the 4R Stadium in Ba.

Tawake is urging the fans to come out in large numbers, turn the grounds into a sea of blue, and create history together.

The Fijian Drua will face the NSW Waratahs at 1pm tomorrow at 4R Stadium in Ba.

item.title: Junior Bula Boys chase historic OFC U-16 title against New Zealand
item.description: Fiji’s U-16 footballers will have their eyes on creating history when they face defending champions New Zealand in the final of the OFC U-16 Men’s Championship in Papue New Guinea tomorrow. The Junior Bula Boys have reached the final for only the third time in the tournament’s history after defeating the Solomon Islands in a dramatic penalty shoot-out in the semi-finals.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji’s U-16 footballers will have their eyes on creating history when they face defending champions New Zealand in the final of the OFC U-16 Men’s Championship in Papue New Guinea tomorrow.

The Junior Bula Boys have reached the final for only the third time in the tournament’s history after defeating the Solomon Islands in a dramatic penalty shoot-out in the semi-finals.

The victory has also secured Fiji's qualification for the FIFA U-17 World Cup 2027.

Fiji last reached the final in 2024, where they were beaten 3-1 by New Zealand.

Fiji have impressed throughout the tournament and are yet to concede a goal, showing strong defensive organisation and determination on their way to the final.

Coach Sunil Kumar says he is proud of the character shown by his players in the closely contested semi-final.

Kumar says they have taken it one step at a time, and experiencing a competition like this for the first time has been great for the young players.

Standing in Fiji’s way are 11-time champions New Zealand, who are chasing a record-extending 12th OFC U-16 Men’s Championship title.

The Junior All Whites coach Martin Bullock says his side has had to work hard throughout the tournament, with teams making every match challenging.

He says his team’s depth has been a major advantage during the competition.

With both teams already qualified for the FIFA U-17 World Cup 2027, the focus now turns to one final challenge: lifting the OFC U-16 Men’s Championship trophy.

The OFC U-16 Men's Championship final between Fiji and New Zealand will be played at 9.30pm tomorrow at PNG Football Stadium in Port Moresby.

item.title: Only defeat or injury will stop Joshua vs Fury fight, says Hearn
item.description: The two former world heavyweight champions are both back in the ring this weekend in what are being seen as must-win warm-up fights before their expected "Battle of Britain". Fury will face Poland's Mariusz Wach in Pattaya, Thailand, while Joshua takes on Albania's Kristian Prenga in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.
item.content:encoded:
The two former world heavyweight champions are both back in the ring this weekend in what are being seen as must-win warm-up fights before their expected "Battle of Britain".

Fury will face Poland's Mariusz Wach in Pattaya, Thailand, while Joshua takes on Albania's Kristian Prenga in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

Although the date and venue for their proposed November fight are yet to be confirmed, it is expected to be the first time the British rivals finally meet after years of failed negotiations.

Fury recently told Sky Sports he was prepared to fight "somebody else" later this year, raising doubts about whether the highly anticipated clash would happen.

However, Hearn rejected those comments, saying Joshua has never pulled out of a fight and pointing out that Fury previously withdrew from their planned bout because of an arbitration ruling involving Deontay Wilder.

Hearn says the only thing likely to prevent the fight from going ahead in November is if either boxer loses or suffers an injury in their fights this weekend.

Joshua's fight will be his first professional bout since a car crash in Nigeria in December claimed the lives of his long-time rehabilitation coach Sina Ghami and close friend and personal trainer Latif "Latz" Ayodele.

Speaking to the BBC, Joshua admitted he is still struggling to come to terms with their deaths, saying the pain remains and he keeps himself busy because he is not yet ready to fully process his grief.

Tomorrow's fight will also be Joshua's first competitive bout since his knockout defeat to IBF world heavyweight champion Daniel Dubois in September 2024.

item.title: Two national team setbacks drive Qaqa ahead of first Commonwealth Games
item.description: Qaqa will represent Fiji in the men's 110 metres hurdles at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games. He began his athletics journey competing in the high jump and long jump while attending LDS Church College in Tamavua before switching to hurdles after moving to Liahona High School in Tonga.
item.content:encoded:
Qaqa will represent Fiji in the men's 110 metres hurdles at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games.

He began his athletics journey competing in the high jump and long jump while attending LDS Church College in Tamavua before switching to hurdles after moving to Liahona High School in Tonga.

Qaqa says the disappointment of missing national selection twice continues to motivate him to train harder and improve.

Speaking to fijivillage News, he says preparations have been the toughest of his career because he will be competing at a much higher level, but the support of his teammates has helped him through the demanding training sessions.

He says the increased intensity of training has prepared the team to compete against some of the Commonwealth's best athletes.

Qaqa , who has paternal links to Qamea and maternal links to Naceva in Kadavu, says he is excited to represent Fiji at his first Commonwealth Games.

His main goal is to progress as far as possible in the competition, with hopes of advancing from the heats into the semi-finals and possibly the final.

He is also aiming to improve his personal best as he prepares for the Pacific Games in Tahiti next year.

Qaqa is encouraging young people to continue working towards their dreams, saying hard work can help them represent Fiji and achieve even greater success in the future.

The Glasgow Commonwealth Games will kick off today and end on the 2nd of August.

Qaqa will compete in the men's 110 metres hurdles during the evening session in Glasgow on Monday, 27th July. The event will be held from 5.30am to 9am on Tuesday, 28th of July.
